title: Add experiment/variant breakdown for TTFT + end-to-end latency metrics (w/ cardinality guardrails)
author: Caleb Johnson
description: This PR adds experiment/variant dimensional breakdowns for request latency metrics emitted from the API gateway, specifically time-to-first-token (TTFT) and end-to-end latency (E2E) for both streaming and non-streaming responses. The intent is to let Console A/B testing results compare latency distributions between variants without requiring per-request tracing or high-cardinality joins. Key points: (1) New metric dimensions: experiment_id and variant_id are attached when a request is assigned to an experiment; when not in an experiment, metrics remain unchanged. (2) Cardinality guardrails: dimensions are allowlisted and we explicitly do NOT attach request_id/user_id/tenant_id/model_name or raw route strings; experiment_id is stable/low-cardinality and variant_id is small (A/B/...). (3) Metric definitions: TTFT is measured as first-byte for non-streaming and as first token chunk for streaming; E2E is measured to last byte written (or error/timeout). (4) Failure safety: if assignment info is missing/invalid, we emit the baseline metrics with no experiment dimensions, and we drop any tag values that fail validation. (5) Backwards compatibility: existing dashboards that query the undimensioned metrics continue to work. Follow-ups: results aggregation PR will consume these metrics keyed by experiment_id/variant_id; we’ll also align names with the metrics schema v1 doc once that lands. Related: ENG-2842 (exposure schema/ingestion) and ENG-2845 (dashboards/alerts); assignment comes from the gateway integration already in-flight.
commits: gateway/metrics: plumb experiment assignment into request context
gateway/metrics: emit ttft_ms and e2e_latency_ms with experiment_id/variant_id dims
telemetry: add tag allowlist + validation for experiment dimensions
telemetry: tests for streaming TTFT measurement and tag dropping
docs: internal notes on metric semantics + edge cases
notable_diff_snippets: New metrics emitted from gateway (names unchanged; just additional dimensions when applicable): telemetry.histogram("gateway.request.ttft_ms", tags={experiment_id, variant_id}) telemetry.histogram("gateway.request.e2e_latency_ms", tags={experiment_id, variant_id})
Tag guardrail example: if experiment_id is not in [a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64} -> drop tag and log once per minute (rate-limited).
review_conversation: Logan Wright (Telemetry/Analytics): Can we confirm the exact semantics for TTFT in streaming? Specifically: first chunk written vs first token event. We need consistency with Console definitions.

Caleb Johnson (author): For streaming we measure to the first token chunk flushed (first write on the streaming response writer after headers). For non-streaming it’s first byte of the response body. I added comments in streaming_tracker.go and a test that asserts TTFT < E2E for a simulated 3-chunk stream.

Allison Grant (SRE/Observability): Cardinality: please do NOT include route or model as a metric dimension in v1; we’ve been burned by this before. Also need an allowlist enforcement so someone can’t accidentally add request headers later.

Caleb Johnson (author): Agreed. This PR introduces pkg/telemetry/metrics/tags_allowlist.go. It rejects any tag key not explicitly allowlisted for these histograms. For experiment breakdown we only allow experiment_id and variant_id. Route stays in the existing per-route dashboards via separate route-labeled metrics (unchanged).
Mina Haddad (Routing): What happens if assignment is computed after we start timing? Could we miss tags for some requests and skew A/B results?

Caleb Johnson (author): Assignment context is attached during routing decision prior to request execution; metrics middleware reads it at emit time. If it’s missing (e.g., internal error), we emit baseline metrics without experiment dims. That should be rare and shows up as a mismatch between exposures and metric volume; ENG-2842/2844 aggregation work can sanity-check that.
Jordan Lee (Policy/Assignment): Please validate variant_id values; we had a staging bug where variant labels included the full config name and blew up tag cardinality.

Caleb Johnson (author): Added validation: variant_id must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$ and is additionally checked against the experiment assignment’s declared variants (if available). Otherwise tag is dropped. Added a regression test modeled after the staging issue.
Allison Grant (SRE/Observability): Request: add a brief changelog entry and confirm no new metrics are emitted when not in an experiment (to avoid doubling series).

Caleb Johnson (author): Added changelog/unreleased/ab-latency-metrics.md and confirmed behavior: same histogram names; tags only appear when experiment assignment is present. Baseline series remains as-is.
Logan Wright (Telemetry/Analytics): Looks good. One more: please ensure time units are ms and buckets remain unchanged so existing alert thresholds don’t break.
Caleb Johnson (author): Confirmed ms across the board; buckets unchanged (see histograms.go).
Allison Grant (SRE/Observability): Approved (thanks for the allowlist).
release_notes: Internal: Gateway latency histograms (TTFT + E2E) now include experiment_id/variant_id dimensions when a request is part of a route-level A/B experiment. No behavior change for non-experiment traffic; added tag allowlist/validation to prevent cardinality blowups.
